articles.desc: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra called on non-banking finance companies and housing finance companies to bolster cybersecurity measures. He emphasized the importance of a comprehensive, risk-based approach to managing cyber threats. Malhotra also highlighted the necessity for responsible credit growth and customer prioritization within these financial institutions. Participants exchanged feedback on policy and operational aspects affecting the NBFC sector during the meeting.

articles.desc: Deepak Parekh addressed the Data Users Conference highlighting the lack of official housing start data in India. He emphasized that this data is crucial due to strong linkages with many allied industries. Parekh noted the recent revision of the GDP base year to 2022-23 and its implications for economic indicators. He also mentioned the importance of high-frequency indicators in assessing economic trends beyond quarterly GDP figures.

articles.title: India weighs 20% export duty on select rice varieties to boost domestic supply
articles.desc: India is contemplating the imposition of export duties on specific rice varieties to improve domestic supplies. This measure aims to mitigate rising prices faced by consumers and industries in the local market. Although the export duty might slow rice exports, it is unlikely to halt shipments completely due to competitive pricing. The poultry and cattle feed sectors have been notably affected by the surge in broken rice prices.

articles.title: NSEL releases Rs 1,950 crore in one-time settlement, ends 14-year payment default
articles.desc: The National Spot Exchange Ltd has revealed a substantial settlement payout of Rs 1,950 crore to eligible claimants, marking the end of a lengthy 14-year legal battle stemming from a Rs 5,600 crore payment crisis. This settlement received the green light from the Mumbai bench of the National Company Law Tribunal, buoyed by considerable backing from claimants.

This investment will contribute to its target of increasing passenger capacity from 96 million to 200 million. The company operates eight airports, handling about 95.3 million passengers in the last fiscal year. The funds will support modernizing existing infrastructure and developing airport cities for commercial activities.

articles.title: Nasdaq futures surge 3% as battered AI stocks gain ground
articles.desc: US stock futures showed a significant rebound on Monday after sharp declines in recent weeks. Investor interest is returning to AI-linked stocks following corrected valuations in the market. Chip stocks led this recovery, with major companies like Nvidia and AMD experiencing notable gains. Analysts remain cautious about confirming a sustainable recovery amid pervasive market concerns.

articles.title: Rupee reversal, debt supply drag India bonds in holiday-shortened week
articles.desc: Indian government bonds fell after the rupee lost its positive momentum against the dollar on Monday. A recent debt sale raised concerns about supply when the Indian states auctioned bonds at higher yields. The rupee also ended down 0.3%, reflecting increased dollar demand from large corporations. Benchmark Brent crude oil prices remained close to $92 a barrel, raising inflation concerns in India.

articles.desc: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the 11th pre-Budget consultation focused on research and education. This meeting was part of the preparations for the upcoming Union Budget 2027-28. Notably, significant allocations were made in the previous Budget for research, innovation and higher education. Earlier, another meeting was held with health and social sector experts for the same purpose.

articles.title: How Nvidia's billion-dollar turnaround in China is threatened by Huang's exit
articles.desc: Nvidia products used to run AI models powering everything from business software to humanoid robots have found growing demand in China from universities, companies and research institutes, even as the US chipmaker's most advanced AI processors remain largely off limits, according to people in the industry and a Reuters review of more than 100 Chinese corporate disclosures and procurement records.

articles.desc: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code reforms are underway, emphasizing the need for responsiveness to economic dynamics. Corporate Affairs Secretary Pallavi Jain Govil stressed the importance of promptly implementing approved insolvency resolution plans. Creditors have recovered Rs 4.30 lakh crore through these plans, highlighting their effectiveness. IBBI officials noted that litigation significantly contributes to delays in the resolution process.

Rupee retreats with stocks as rally takes a breather, positive bias lingers
articles.desc: After a five-day rise, the Indian rupee faced a setback on Monday, driven by heightened dollar demand from major corporations. This shift in momentum was compounded by profit-taking activities. The rupee settled at 92.91 against the dollar, following a peak of 92.44. Additionally, underwhelming local stock performance fueled a bearish outlook for the rupee. Nevertheless, analysts predict a sustained positive sentiment towards stocks and currencies amid ongoing evaluations.

articles.title: German bond yields edge higher as equity rebound eases safe-haven demand
articles.desc: Germany's government bond yields increased marginally on Monday as equity markets began to rebound, leading to diminished interest in safe-haven assets. In the wake of a difficult week for stocks, investors indicated a readiness to engage with riskier assets. The yield on 10-year German bonds rose by 2 basis points, signaling a fall in bond prices.

This consultation is a significant step in preparing for the Union Budget 2027-28. Prior meetings have included various sectors, covering agriculture, manufacturing, and health. The government allocated more funds to healthcare in the previous budget, marking a 10 percent increase.

articles.title: India to be one of APAC champions with 7% GDP forecast for FY27, but El Nino will prove costly: S&P
articles.desc: S&P Global Ratings projects a robust 7 percent GDP growth for India in the current and upcoming fiscal years. However, the impact of El Nino is anticipated to drive food prices higher, thus increasing inflationary pressures. With input costs on the rise, these expenses are likely to be transferred to consumers.

articles.title: India bonds give up marginal opening gains as profit booking takes over
articles.desc: Indian government bonds fell after initial gains due to profit booking by traders and a sharp rupee decline. The benchmark yield of the 6.94% 2036 bond increased to 7.2185% during trading hours. Last week, the yield had dropped significantly due to lower US Treasury yields and a stronger rupee. Investors now focus on the upcoming Reserve Bank of India's policy decision on December 4.

articles.title: Rupee retreats, Goldman calls it a 'port of stability' in AI storm
articles.desc: The Indian rupee initially rose to a seven-month high before retreating amid corporate dollar buying. It is on track for a monthly gain of over 2%, bolstered by significant foreign investment in Indian equities. Analysts noted that the rupee's early gains pushed it into overbought territory, prompting some selling. Despite recent fluctuations, the rupee has remained stable compared to other major currencies.

articles.title: India factory demand offsets weaker services growth in November, PMI shows
articles.desc: India's private sector activity experienced marginal growth in November, driven by manufacturing demand and production. The HSBC Flash India Composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose slightly from October, indicating continued expansion. The manufacturing sector achieved a nine-month high, while the services sector saw a decline in growth. Employment trends diverged, with factories increasing hiring and services sectors reducing jobs. Companies exhibited optimism about future performance, although confidence remained below historic averages.
